record.paper_title: Open problems in membrane computing and how not to solve them
record.original_question: For P-system variants in which an isolated single membrane working in polynomial time has only P computational power, can the internal behavior of each membrane be replaced by a polynomial-time Turing-machine simulation so that all additional power beyond P comes solely from membrane division, communication, and the resulting network structure? A key subproblem is whether a single charged membrane can feasibly count exponentially many identical objects entering in parallel, effectively converting a unary multiplicity of incoming objects into a binary count.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A P system with active membranes is a computational device consisting of a hierarchy of nested membranes; each membrane carries an electrical charge (positive, negative, or neutral) and contains a multiset of objects drawn from a finite alphabet. Computation proceeds in synchronous, maximally parallel steps governed by rules that may rewrite objects, send objects through a membrane (possibly changing its charge), dissolve a membrane, or divide a membrane into two copies. A "single-membrane" P system is one whose membrane structure consists of just one membrane (the skin); in many variants, such isolated single membranes working in polynomial time are known to characterize exactly the class P.

Question. Consider the family of P-system variants V with the following property: any single, isolated membrane of V running for a polynomially bounded number of steps recognizes only languages in P. Prove or disprove the following uniform reduction claim:

(A) For every variant V in this family, there exists a polynomial-time deterministic Turing machine simulator M such that the global behavior of any P system Π in V on any input is equivalent to the system obtained by replacing the internal evolution of each individual membrane of Π by M; that is, all computational power of V beyond P arises solely from membrane division, inter-membrane communication, and the resulting network structure of membranes.

Sub-question (counting). As a key special case, decide whether the following is possible in deterministic polynomial time per step on a single charged membrane: given a multiset over a one-letter alphabet {a} entering the membrane in parallel with multiplicity n (where n may be exponential in the input size, encoded in unary by the parallel arrival of n copies of a), produce inside the membrane a binary representation of n using only standard rules of P systems with active membranes (object rewriting, communication, and charge changes) that operate in polynomial time. Equivalently: can a single charged membrane feasibly "count" an exponential number of identical objects arriving simultaneously, converting their unary multiplicity into a binary numeral?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on space complexity in P systems with active membranes (e.g., the Journal of Membrane Computing articles from 2021–2022 on alternative/binary space measures) explicitly notes that it remains unresolved whether efficient (binary) encoding of object multiplicities strictly increases computational power over the natural unary encoding for the standard variants. No proof of the uniform Turing-machine reduction, nor of the single-membrane exponential counting capability, has been reported; the question is still treated as open in the membrane-computing literature.

status_evidence.title: Evaluating space measures in P systems
status_evidence.snippet: Computational classes defined using binary space do not differ from those using the original definition for the standard variants examined; it remains open to exhibit a class where the difference manifests.
status_evidence.claim: The binary-vs-unary counting/space question in P systems is acknowledged as open in recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Alternative space definitions for P systems with active membranes
status_evidence.snippet: Considers a hypothetical silico implementation allowing storage of object multiplicity using binary numbers versus unary biochemical implementation.
status_evidence.claim: The status of efficient counting and the role of single-membrane internal power versus network structure remains a topic of ongoing investigation.
